properties.natural_language: Before any JSON-RPC request is processed by the Execution Layer, the request body MUST be parsed as valid JSON; malformed JSON MUST result in error code -32700 and no method execution.

Before method dispatch, every JSON-RPC request received from an untrusted client MUST have its structure validated (jsonrpc, method, id fields present) and method name checked against the supported method table; unknown methods MUST return error code -32601.

Before method execution, all RPC parameters MUST be validated for correct Quantity (minimal hex, no leading zeros) or Data (even hex pairs, 0x-prefixed) encoding as specified by EIP-1474; invalid encoding MUST return error code -32602.

Before a raw transaction submitted via eth_sendRawTransaction is added to the transaction pool, the hex-encoded data MUST be decoded, RLP-parsed, and its ECDSA signature MUST be verified to recover a valid sender address.

Before a transaction enters the pool from the JSON-RPC boundary, its fee structure MUST satisfy: maxFeePerGas >= block baseFeePerGas AND maxPriorityFeePerGas <= maxFeePerGas; violations MUST raise appropriate exceptions.

Before processing any wire protocol message from a P2P peer, the message type MUST be checked against the eth/67 supported set; deprecated GetNodeData (0x0d) and NodeData (0x0e) messages MUST be rejected.
Before accepting a block from a P2P peer, the block header MUST be fully validated including parent hash, timestamp, gas limit, and all Shanghai/Prague-specific fields.

Before accepting a block from a peer, the excess_blob_gas header field MUST be independently recalculated using the EIP-7918 reserve price conditional logic and MUST match the header value exactly; any mismatch MUST cause block rejection.

Before a block producer's excess_blob_gas value is accepted, validators MUST independently compute the reserve price using BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas / GAS_PER_BLOB and verify the correct pricing mode (reserve vs normal) was applied.

Before applying the excess blob gas calculation, the system MUST evaluate the reserve condition (BLOB_BASE_COST * parent.base_fee > GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_base_fee) using parent block data and select the correct formula path.

Before any Beacon API request is processed, an infrastructure-level security layer (reverse proxy, firewall) SHOULD be present to authenticate and rate-limit requests; without such a layer, all API endpoints are exposed to DoS attacks.
Before processing Beacon API requests, the system MUST parse the HTTP request, route it to the correct OpenAPI-defined handler, and return a proper 404 response for unmatched routes.

Before a prover signs an execution proof received from the proof engine at /eth/v1/prover/execution_proofs, the prover MUST validate the proof engine output to ensure the proof is cryptographically sound; signing an invalid proof could deceive stateless validators.
Before a prover signs a proof, domain separation MUST be applied using DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF and the current epoch to prevent cross-domain signature replay attacks.

Before accepting a SignedExecutionProof from the P2P gossip network, the full validation pipeline MUST be executed: non-empty proof data check, proof engine cryptographic verification, duplicate detection by request root + proof type, and BLS signature verification against whitelisted prover public keys.
Before a gossip-received execution proof is accepted, the submitter's public key MUST be verified against the whitelisted prover registry; proofs from non-whitelisted participants MUST be rejected.

Before the execution engine processes a forkchoiceUpdated call, the Engine API connection MUST be JWT-authenticated; the fork choice update containing head_block_hash, safe_block_hash, and finalized_block_hash MUST be processed atomically.

Before suppressing a fork choice update for proposer re-org protection, ALL 8 conditions of should_override_forkchoice_update MUST be simultaneously true: head_late, proposing_reorg_slot, FFG_competitive, finalization_ok, weak_head, strong_parent, and related timing conditions.

Before validating the merge transition, the terminal PoW block fetched via eth_getBlockByHash MUST satisfy: total_difficulty >= TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY AND parent_total_difficulty < TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY; alternatively, if TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH is set, the execution payload parent hash MUST match exactly.

When PoW block data is unavailable during merge transition validation, the system MUST defer block processing for later reprocessing rather than rejecting the block; this ensures graceful degradation when the execution client is not yet synced.

The sync committee key aggregation optimization path MUST use strictly greater than 256 out of 512 participants as the threshold for the subtraction-based aggregation; exactly 256 participants MUST use the direct aggregation path.

Before applying inactivity score decrements, the system MUST apply both sequential decrements: first subtract min(1, score) if the chain is not in an inactivity leak, then always subtract min(INACTIVITY_SCORE_RECOVERY_RATE=16, score), allowing up to 17 points decrease per epoch.

A validator that has been slashed between sync committee selection and duty period MUST still appear in the committee but MUST NOT receive participation rewards; they MUST receive non-participation penalties.

The RANDAO seed used for sync committee selection MUST be derived from a sufficiently past epoch (EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD + 1 epochs ago) to prevent attackers from biasing committee composition through RANDAO manipulation.
An attacker controlling fewer than 2/3 of sync committee members MUST NOT be able to produce a valid aggregate BLS signature over a false block root, ensuring light client security.

The reserve price check MUST be evaluated every block using the parent block's data; transitions between reserve and normal pricing modes MUST be smooth with no discontinuity in the excess_blob_gas calculation.
All execution clients MUST implement the identical conditional excess_blob_gas calculation with reserve price logic; any divergence between client implementations would cause consensus failures.

Endpoints that trigger heavy computation (state queries, validator duties) or return large responses (full beacon state) MUST be treated as primary DoS vectors; rate limiting SHOULD be applied at the infrastructure level.

Before trusting Beacon API client requests, operators MUST ensure the API is not exposed to the public internet without security layers; a malicious API client could manipulate validator behavior causing slashing or missed attestations.

The prover whitelist mechanism MUST ensure only authorized entities can submit execution proofs that are accepted by the network; the governance process for whitelisting MUST be defined before production deployment.

Sufficient whitelisted provers MUST be online and generating proofs for every block in a timely manner; if no proof is available, stateless validators MUST fall back to full execution client mode rather than skipping validation.

An eth/67 client receiving a deprecated GetNodeData (0x0d) or NodeData (0x0e) message MUST reject or ignore the message; the specific rejection behavior (silent drop vs peer disconnect) is implementation-defined.
Valid transaction type bytes MUST be limited to: 0 (legacy), 1 (EIP-2930), 2 (EIP-1559), 3 (EIP-4844), and 4 (EIP-7702); any other type byte MUST trigger a TransactionTypeError.
Blob transactions (type 3) MUST NOT be allowed to create contracts; any type-3 transaction with to=None MUST raise TransactionTypeContractCreationError.

The 'same transaction' check for SELFDESTRUCT eligibility MUST include all contract creation contexts within the transaction, including internal CREATE and CREATE2 calls, not only direct deployment transactions.

For contracts created via CREATE2 that are destroyed and re-created at the same address within the same transaction, each creation event MUST reset the same-transaction flag, allowing subsequent SELFDESTRUCT to function with full deletion behavior.

Ethereum node filters created via eth_newFilter, eth_newBlockFilter, or eth_newPendingTransactionFilter MUST be automatically destroyed after a timeout period to prevent resource leaks; a 5-minute default timeout is recommended.
The 'pending' block identifier behavior is implementation-specific; security analysis MUST account for the fact that different clients may return different results for pending state queries.
The consensus client MUST monitor TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY via the execution engine API and MUST NOT call merge transition functions until the PoW chain has met the difficulty threshold.

After successful BLS fast aggregate signature verification of a SyncAggregate, the system MUST distribute rewards to participating sync committee members (SYNC_COMMITTEE_WEIGHT=2/64 of total rewards / 512 / 32 per slot) and penalize non-participants equally.
After sync aggregate validation succeeds, the block proposer MUST receive an additional reward proportional to PROPOSER_WEIGHT / (WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR - PROPOSER_WEIGHT).

After attestation processing, the participation flags (TIMELY_SOURCE, TIMELY_TARGET, TIMELY_HEAD) MUST be set in epoch_participation for each attesting validator based on timeliness: source within integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH), target within SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, head in immediately next slot.

After epoch boundary processing, inactivity scores MUST be updated: increment by INACTIVITY_SCORE_BIAS (4) for validators missing target, decrease by min(1, score) if not in inactivity leak, and always decrease by min(INACTIVITY_SCORE_RECOVERY_RATE=16, score).

After inactivity penalty computation, non-target participants MUST receive a penalty of effective_balance * inactivity_score / (INACTIVITY_SCORE_BIAS * INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT=50331648), resulting in quadratic penalty growth for sustained inactivity.

After a sync committee period boundary (every 256 epochs), the system MUST rotate committees: move next_sync_committee to current_sync_committee and compute a new next committee using RANDAO seed from EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD + 1 epochs ago.
After SELFDESTRUCT executes on a contract created in the same transaction, the contract's storage, code, and account data MUST be fully deleted and its balance transferred to the target address.
After SELFDESTRUCT executes on a pre-existing contract (not created in same TX), the contract code and storage MUST persist; only the balance MUST be transferred to the target address.
After a same-TX-created contract executes SELFDESTRUCT targeting itself, Ether MUST be permanently burned (removed from circulation); pre-existing contracts targeting themselves MUST NOT burn Ether.

After blob transaction validation completes, the system MUST have verified: at least one blob is present, all versioned hashes have correct version prefix, blob gas does not exceed block limit, and maxFeePerBlobGas >= current blob base fee.
After the EIP-7918 fork activation block, new blobSchedule parameters from EIP-7840 MUST be immediately active; the reserve price mechanism MUST apply from the first post-fork block.

After successful merge transition validation, the system MUST transition to post-merge state where the beacon chain manages all execution payloads and PoW is no longer the canonical execution mechanism.
After a forkchoiceUpdated call is processed, all execution payloads up to finalized_block_hash MUST be irreversibly persisted; the execution chain MUST be reorganized to match the consensus head.

After a prover signs an execution proof with BLS using DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, the SignedExecutionProof MUST be broadcast on the execution_proof gossip topic for network-wide propagation to stateless validators.

After upgrading to eth/67, the client MUST NOT process GetNodeData (0x0d) or NodeData (0x0e) message types; state sync functionality MUST use snap protocol (GetByteCodes 0x04, GetTrieNodes 0x06) instead.
State transitions in the Shanghai fork MUST be atomic: either fully complete or fully revert. Partial state corruption MUST NOT occur during transaction processing or fork application.
All clients MUST have upgraded to Shanghai-compatible software at the activation block; blocks processed under Shanghai rules MUST be rejected by pre-Shanghai clients and vice versa.

After a transaction passes all validation checks (signature, nonce, balance, fee structure), it MUST be executed in the EVM; failed validation MUST result in transaction rejection without any state changes.

Every JSON-RPC request MUST result in exactly one response: either a result object on success or an error object with a standardized error code (-32700 through -32005); no request may be silently dropped.
After authorization list validation for EIP-7702 transactions, the list MUST contain at least one entry; an empty authorization list MUST cause the transaction to be rejected.
After init code size validation during contract creation, code exceeding MAX_INITCODE_SIZE MUST be rejected; only init code within size limits proceeds to execution.
When an eth/67-only peer is encountered, state data retrieval MUST use snap protocol GetByteCodes (0x04) for contract code and GetTrieNodes (0x06) for trie nodes; GetNodeData MUST NOT be attempted.

The RPC transport layer (HTTP/WebSocket) MUST provide sufficient protection for sensitive operations like eth_sign; node operators MUST NOT expose signing methods without TLS to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.
Gas refunds MUST NOT be issued for SELFDESTRUCT calls on pre-existing contracts (non-same-transaction context); EIP-2929 access list gas rules MUST apply in all cases.
The removal of GetNodeData in eth/67 MUST NOT create new attack vectors compared to the snap protocol; the security properties of state sync MUST remain equivalent or stronger.
